full_judgment:
7. I have perused the judgments of the Courts below. The trial Court came to a finding that the plaintiffs were able to prove their title in the suit land on the basis of Amalnama Exhibit-1 and the Hukumnama Exhibit-2. The learned Assistant Judge further came to a finding that S.A. Khatian in respect of the suit land was prepared and published in the name of the plaintiff's father and that Exhibit-4, the report of Advocate Commissioner proved that the plaintiffs had their homestead on the suit land. The trial Court also found that the plaintiffs possessed the suit land till 1387 and that thereafter, they were dispossessed there from. The trial court found that defendant No. 1 could not prove the settlement of his vendor, Munshi Sk. from whom he purchased .11 acre of land on 4.1.1963. Therefore, the trial Court held that defendant No. 1 could not derive any title in the suit land on the basis of his purchase. 

 8. The appellate court, on the other hand, came to a finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their settlement in the suit land on the basis of 1 and 2. The appellate Court held that Exhibits 1 and 2 revealed that those were created recently for the purpose of the suit. The appellate Court found that Exhibits 1 and 2 were not proved by any employee of Ambaria Zamindari Estate. Therefore, the appellate Court disbelieved Exhibits 1 and 2. The appellate court found that defendant No.1 produced the registered sale deed dated 4.1.1963 (Exhibit-Ka) to show that he purchased .11 acre of land from Munshi Sk. who was alleged to have taken settlement of .22 acre of land from Ambaria Zamindari Estate. The appellate Court found that the R.S. Khatian has not been prepared either in the names of the plaintiffs or in the name of defendant No. 1.
